request.spec:
Periods can be generated: a from-date and a to-date and a button create one period per calendar
month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each running from the first to the last
day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), named yyyy-mm, each written as PERIOD_ADDED.
A month whose name is already a period, or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out
and the others are still made. Show how many were made. A to-date before the from-date is refused
with an error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Periods can be generated: a from-date and a to-date and a button create one period per calendar
month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each running from the first to the last
day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), named yyyy-mm, each written as PERIOD_ADDED.
A month whose name is already a period, or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out
and the others are still made. Show how many were made. A to-date before the from-date is refused
with an error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Monthly period generation is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests on the first run.

**How it works**
- **New endpoint:** `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate`, defined in `rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate.POST.yml`. It follows the same step-by-step pattern as adding a single period: viewers are refused first, then the dates are checked, the periods stored, the audit written, and the count returned.
- **What it makes:** one period per month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, named yyyy-mm and running from the 1st to the last day of the month (so February ends on the 28th or 29th). Any month whose name is already used, or whose days overlap an existing period, is left out and the rest are still made. Each new period writes its own `PERIOD_ADDED` line in month order, in the same format as a manually added period.
- **Refusals:** a to-date before the from-date, or a value that isn't a date, is refused with an error. Nothing is stored and nothing is written to the audit file.
- **Screen:** the Periods panel now has a second form with `period-generate-from`, `period-generate-to` and a `period-generate` button. After each press it shows how many were made in `period-generated`; the old count is cleared when you press again. Errors show in `period-generate-error`.

A blank date in the form is filled in with the sheet's today before it is sent, so the server always receives both dates. The tests always fill both, so that default is untested.

The new server-side classes are in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/period/`, and the form is in `src/main/frontend/features/periods/periods.slot.tsx`. No database change was needed.
